gaps: pool_idle, pool acquire-wait histograms and per-endpoint/route connection metrics were not queried (final query_metric call returned budget_exhausted, ev_13).
No log content search was performed to identify which request path or query held connections; the search_logs and second log_patterns calls returned budget_exhausted (ev_15, ev_14).
A further metric query planned after the main set returned budget_exhausted (ev_16), so no additional signals (e.g. CPU, memory, connection counts by endpoint) were checked.
Windows before 10:40:00 were not queried, so it is unknown whether pool_used was at zero for long prior to the window or whether a similar slow climb occurred earlier.
Deployment/config change events for version 1.0.1 were not checked; the link to a code change is inferred, not verified.
DB-side connection counts, slow-query logs and the possibility of connections held by other clients were not examined.
report.summary: The most probable cause is connection-pool exhaustion: the fixed pool filled while request rate stayed flat, queued requests then timed out at connect time, producing 5xx errors and a p95 latency jump. Database operation latency and event-loop delay stayed flat throughout, so neither DB slowness, traffic surge nor CPU/event-loop saturation explains the failure. The user-facing SLO breaches are downstream effects of pool saturation.

timeline.event: Baseline: pool_used at {pool_used_first} connections, pool_max fixed at {pool_max_min}, request_rate near {rr_first} req/s.
pool_used is climbing ({pool_used_early} connections) while request_rate and db_operation_p95 remain flat.
Pool saturation: pool_used hits the ceiling of {pool_used_max} connections and pool_pending jumps to {pending_max} queued requests.
First "timeout exceeded when trying to connect" error log line, after the pool saturated.
latency_p95 jumps to {lat_last} s, error_ratio_5xx is {err_first}, pool_timeout_rate {timeout_first} timeouts/s.
Detection fires: latency_p95 peaks at {lat_max} s, error_ratio_5xx at {err_max}, pool_timeout_rate at {timeout_max} timeouts/s, pool_pending still {pending_last}.

hypotheses.statement: A code path began holding DB connections without releasing them (or far longer than the DB operation time), draining the fixed pool of {pool_max_min} connections; requests then queued (pool_pending reaching {pending_max}) and failed with connect timeouts ("timeout exceeded when trying to connect", {p1_count} occurrences), producing the 5xx ratio {err_max} and p95 latency {lat_max}.
Application CPU/event-loop saturation caused the latency and error spike. Ruled out: eventloop_delay_p99 peaked at {el_max} s while requests waited on the pool.
The database itself became slow, holding connections. Ruled out: db_operation_p95 stayed between {db_min} s and {db_max} s while the pool saturated.
A traffic surge exhausted the pool. Ruled out: request_rate remained between {rr_first} req/s and {rr_max} req/s across the window.

observations.statement: pool_used climbed steadily from {pool_used_first} connections at the start of the window to the pool ceiling of {pool_used_max} connections at 10:44:00.403Z and stayed there through the end of the window ({pool_used_last}).
pool_max was constant at {pool_max_min} connections across all points of the window, so the pool size is a fixed ceiling rather than an autoscaling limit.
pool_pending was {pending_min} queued requests until 10:43:45, then jumped to {pending_max} at 10:44:00.403Z and was still {pending_last} at the end of the window, i.e. waiters never drained.

The dominant error log pattern is "request failed" with exception "timeout exceeded when trying to connect", appearing {p1_count} times between 10:44:13.766Z and 10:44:30.655Z, i.e. after the pool saturated.
pool_timeout_rate reached {timeout_max} timeouts/s at 10:44:30.403Z, after {timeout_first} timeouts/s at 10:44:15.403Z.
latency_p95 was flat near {lat_min} s for the early points of the window, then jumped to {lat_last} s at 10:44:15.403Z and {lat_max} s at 10:44:30.403Z.
error_ratio_5xx rose from {err_first} at 10:44:15.403Z to {err_max} at 10:44:30.403Z.

Error-level log volume was absent during the baseline window ending at 10:42:15.403Z (only warn and info lines: {base_warn_sum} warn, {base_info_sum} info) and then totalled {err_sum} error lines in the incident window, concentrated in the last minute ({err_last} lines in the 10:45 bucket).
db_operation_p95 stayed essentially flat between {db_min} s and {db_max} s across the whole window, showing no database slowdown.
request_rate stayed in a narrow band: first {rr_first} req/s, max {rr_max} req/s, last {rr_last} req/s, so there was no traffic surge when the pool filled.
eventloop_delay_p99 peaked at only {el_max} s and ended at {el_last} s, indicating the application event loop was not saturated while requests queued on the pool.

recommendations.action: Restart demo-service (version 1.0.1) to drop the leaked connections and clear the queued waiters, then confirm pool_used and pool_pending return to baseline.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_1: pool_used stayed pinned at the fixed ceiling and waiters never drained; a restart releases held connections as an immediate mitigation.

recommendations.action: Audit pool-acquire/release code paths and any changes shipped in version 1.0.1 around 10:42–10:43 for missing release in error branches or connections held across awaits.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_1: the pool drained in about a minute at constant load with flat DB latency, pointing to a leak rather than slow queries.

recommendations.action: Add pool instrumentation and alerting (pool_used/pool_max ratio, pool_pending, pool_timeout_rate) with a warning well before saturation, and emit a warning log when a connection is held beyond a threshold.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_1: pool saturation preceded the SLO breach, but only latency and error-ratio alerts fired.

recommendations.action: Evaluate raising pool_max or adding an acquire timeout/backpressure only after the leak is fixed, to avoid masking it.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_1: the fixed ceiling of pool_max converted the leak into total starvation; raising it would delay but not prevent recurrence.
